title: INT 1Ah, the time, sound and PCI services
covers: INT 1Ah: the system clock and RTC services, the PCjr and Tandy digital sound calls, and the PCI BIOS functions.

rows.text: AH=00h gets the system time: CX:DX are the clock ticks since midnight.
AL is the midnight flag, nonzero if midnight has passed since the time was last read.
There are about 18.2 ticks a second, 1800B0h a day, except on the Tandy 2000 at 20.
IBM and many clone BIOSes set the flag rather than increment it, losing a day when two midnights pass unpolled.
Because the read clears the flag, an application that reads after midnight before DOS makes DOS advance no date.
Modern MS-DOS and PC DOS releases (5.0+???) treat AL as a day counter, as older releases expect.
DOS 5 to 7.10 offer a SWITCHES=/T option that forces the older flag behaviour.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0x00 of its dispatch on AH.
CX becomes the high word of the 32-bit tick count at 0040:006C.
DX becomes the low word of that tick count.
AH=01h sets the system time from CX:DX, the clock ticks since midnight.
There are about 18.2 ticks a second, 1800B0h a day, except on the Tandy 2000 at 20.
The call resets the midnight-passed flag.
Nothing is returned: AH is left as the caller passed it.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0x01 of its dispatch on AH.
The tick count is written to 0040:006C as a 32-bit value built from CX and DX.
AH=02h gets the time from the real-time clock.
The caller should clear CF before the call, to avoid the bug below.
CF is clear if successful and set on error, the clock not running or mid-update.
CH is the hour, in BCD.
CL is the minutes, in BCD.
DH is the seconds, in BCD.
DL is the daylight savings flag: 00h standard time, 01h daylight time.
The Sperry PC also supports the call, returning binary values with DL always 00h.
MS-DOS and PC DOS use the call to detect a preset RTC, calling once more when the values are nonzero.
Some BIOSes leave CF unchanged on success, so CF should be cleared before the call.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0x02 of its dispatch on AH.
The case first writes CMOS 0Bh for BCD and 24-hour mode, then waits for the update to finish.
It clears CF and lets the CPU idle four times after the reads.
CH receives CMOS register 04h, the hours.
CL receives CMOS register 02h, the minutes.
DH receives CMOS register 00h, the seconds.
DL receives bit 0 of CMOS register 0Bh, the daylight saving bit.
CF is always cleared: the wait cannot fail, so the error the document gives never happens.
AH=03h sets the clock time from CH, CL and DH, in BCD, and DL holds the daylight savings flag.
Nothing is returned: AH is left as the caller passed it.
The Sperry PC also supports the call, in binary rather than BCD, and ignores DL.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0x03 of its dispatch on AH.
The case selects BCD and 24-hour mode, waits, stops updates, writes hours, minutes and seconds to CMOS 04h, 02h and 00h, then allows updates.
The daylight saving bit is written from bit 0 of DH, the seconds, so DL is ignored.
AH=04h gets the date from the real-time clock.
The caller should clear CF before the call, to avoid the bug below.
CF is clear if successful and set on error.
CH is the century, in BCD.
CL is the year, in BCD.
DH is the month, in BCD.
DL is the day, in BCD.
PC DOS 7 plus Y2K fixes and PC DOS 2000 provide similar but not identical means, which cannot be switched off.
MS-DOS and older PC DOS provide no such correction, so a buggy BIOS needs an extra Y2K TSR.
Some BIOSes, such as the Compaq Deskpro EP/SB ROM of 1998/07/25, leave CF unchanged on success.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0x04 of its dispatch on AH.
The case selects BCD and 24-hour mode, waits, then reads century, year, month and day from CMOS 32h, 09h, 08h and 07h.
It clears CF and lets the CPU idle four times after the reads.
CF is always cleared: the wait cannot fail, so the error the document gives never happens.
AH=05h sets the clock date from CH, CL, DH and DL, all in BCD.
Nothing is returned: AH is left as the caller passed it.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0x05 of its dispatch on AH.
The case selects BCD and 24-hour mode, waits, stops updates, writes century, year, month and day to CMOS 32h, 09h, 08h and 07h, then allows updates.

searched.gave: MAME's tree has no PC BIOS INT 1Ah PCI code, and its headers cite no document for the dispatch.
The PCI SIG's BIOS specification documents each AX=B1xx function, not the AH=B1h dispatch.
No PCI BIOS specification was found in the archive's catalogue.
Holds no PCI BIOS specification; the list is the public description of these functions.
Ralf Brown's list has a section per AX=B1xx function and none for the AH=B1h dispatch.

rows.text: INT 1Ah AH=B1h is the PCI BIOS call, the AL of AX selecting the function.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0xB1 of its dispatch on AH.
With the PCI bus disabled the case sets CF and leaves AH as it was.
An AL that no case takes logs an error and sets CF, leaving AH as it was.
AX=B101h with EDI zero checks that the PCI BIOS is installed.
AH is 00h if the BIOS is installed.
CF is clear if the BIOS is installed.
EDX is 20494350h, ' ICP'.
EDI is the physical address of the protected-mode entry point.
AL holds the PCI hardware characteristics.
BH is the PCI interface level major version, in BCD.
BL is the PCI interface level minor version, in BCD.
CL is the number of the last PCI bus in the system.
EAX, EBX, ECX and EDX may be modified, as may all flags except IF.
The call may use up to 1024 bytes of stack, and does not enable disabled interrupts.
Some BIOSes do not change EDI, so applications should zero it before the call.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by the case 0xB1 followed by the case 0x01 on AL.
When the PCI bus is initialised it stores AH 00h, AL 01h, BX 0210h, CX 0000h, the dword 20494350h and the protected-mode entry point.
CF is cleared when the bus is initialised and set when it is not.
AH is left as the caller passed it when the bus is not initialised.
AX=B102h finds the SI-th PCI device with the vendor ID in DX and the device ID in CX.
CF is clear on success and set on error.
AH is the status, one of 00h, 83h or 86h, of which 00h is successful.
BH is the bus number.
BL is the device and function number: bits 7-3 device, bits 2-0 function.
EAX, EBX, ECX and EDX may be modified, as may all flags except IF.
The call may use up to 1024 bytes of stack, and does not enable disabled interrupts.
Device ID FFFFh may be reserved as a wildcard in future implementations.
The meanings of BL and BH were exchanged between the initial drafts and the final implementation.
Devices sharing one vendor and device ID are enumerated by incrementing SI until error 86h.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by the case 0xB1 followed by the case 0x02 on AL.
It asks for device/function numbers 0 to 255 of bus 0 and then one more, comparing CX high and DX low and counting matches until the SI-th.
AH becomes 00h on a match and 86h when none is found.
BH becomes 00h, bus 0.
BL becomes the device number of the match.
CF is cleared on a match and set otherwise.
AX=B103h finds the SI-th PCI device of the class in ECX: class, subclass and programming interface.
CF is clear on success and set on error.
AH is the status: 00h success, 86h device not found.
BH is the bus number.
BL is the device and function number: bits 7-3 device, bits 2-0 function.
EAX, EBX, ECX and EDX may be modified, as may all flags except IF.
The call may use up to 1024 bytes of stack, and does not enable disabled interrupts.
The meanings of BL and BH were exchanged between the initial drafts and the final implementation.
Devices sharing one class code are enumerated by incrementing SI until error 86h.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by the case 0xB1 followed by the case 0x03 on AL.
It scans bus 0's device entries, comparing the class register with the low 24 bits of ECX, and counts matches until the SI-th.
AH becomes 00h on a match and 86h when none is found.
BH becomes 00h, bus 0.
BL becomes the device number of the match.
CF is cleared on a match and set otherwise.
AX=B108h reads a configuration byte: BH is the bus, BL the device and function, DI the register.
CF is clear on success and set on error.
CL is the byte read.
AH is the status, 00h or 87h, of which 00h is successful.
EAX, EBX, ECX and EDX may be modified, as may all flags except IF.
The call may use up to 1024 bytes of stack, and does not enable disabled interrupts.
The meanings of BL and BH on entry were exchanged between the initial drafts and the final implementation.
An Award BIOS 4.51PG of 05/24/96 returns all ones for register 00h when the function number is nonzero.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by the case 0xB1 followed by the case 0x08 on AL.
It writes the register selection to port 0CF8h and reads at 0CFCh plus the low bits of DI.
CL receives the value read.
AH becomes 00h.
CF is cleared; the register number is masked rather than checked.
AH is always 00h; the 87h the document gives for a bad register never happens.

AH=80h sets the sound multiplexer source: AL 00h is 8253 channel 2, 01h cassette, 02h Audio In, 03h the sound generator.
Although documented in the 1000TL Technical Reference, the 1000TL BIOS has just an IRET for this call.
Nothing is returned: the section gives the call no Return line.
The INT 1Ah handler reaches it by case 0x80 of its dispatch on AH.
The case logs the requested source and returns with every register and CF unchanged.
It sets up no multiplexer, so the source AL names is never selected.
AX=8100h is the Tandy digital sound installation check.
AX is 00C4h when the sound is supported, its AL above 80h.
CF is set when the sound chip is busy and clear when it is free.
The value of CF is not definitive: the call is repeated until CF is clear, then AH=84h is called.
The INT 1Ah cases 0x81 to 0x85 share a body that calls TandyDAC_Handler, whose case 0x81 answers.
The handler returns at once when neither a Sound Blaster nor a Tandy DAC is configured.
AX becomes the Tandy DAC port when one exists, else 00C4h.
CF follows Tandy_TransferInProgress, set while a transfer runs.
The port returned is set at initialisation and reset to 0 when the BIOS post sets the sound up.
AH=82h starts recording digital sound to the buffer at ES:BX, CX bytes long, at the rate in DX.
AH is 00h.
CF is set if the sound is busy and clear if the sound chip is free.
The rate should be a tenth of the AH=83h value on the 1000TL, an eleventh and a half on the 1000SL.
AX=8100h and AH=84h should be called before it.
The BIOS issues INT 15/AX=91FBh when the input completes.

AH becomes 00h whether the transfer starts or is refused.
CF is set when a transfer is in progress and cleared otherwise.
It stores the length at 0040:00D0 and the delay with the volume from AL at 0040:00D2.
AH=83h starts playing digital sound from ES:BX, CX bytes, AL the volume, DX the time between samples.
AH is 00h.
CF is set if the sound is busy and clear if the sound chip is free.
The call returns while the sound plays in the background, the chip clocked at 3.57 MHz with DX as the divisor.
The BIOS appears to call INT 15/AX=91FBh on underflow, allowing another call for seamless long sounds.
